## Language rule

All output — code, comments, commit messages, PR descriptions, documentation, and conversation — is **English only**, even if the user prompts in another language.

## Git rules

<!-- IF:no_attribution -->
- **No AI attribution, ever.** Do not add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers, "Generated with …", "Made with AI", or any similar attribution to commit messages or PR descriptions. Commit messages must read as if written by the user alone.
<!-- ENDIF -->
- **Commit style:** conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `test:`).
- **Branching:** work on feature branches (short, descriptive names); merge to main through PRs.
<!-- IF:feature_branches -->
- Never merge your own PR without review or explicit user consent.
<!-- ENDIF -->
- **Never modify git configuration.** Do not run `git config` write commands and never set or change `user.name`, `user.email`, or signing settings. If identity is missing, inform the user and let them set it.
- Only commit when the user asks. Run the tests before every commit.

## Workflow: direct mode

One task at a time, spec-driven. The lifecycle artifacts live in `specs/`:

1. **SPEC** (`specs/SPEC.md`) — what to build: goal, non-goals, acceptance criteria, open questions.
2. **PLAN** (`specs/PLAN.md`) — the task breakdown for the current spec.
3. **TASK** (`specs/TASK.md`) — the one task in progress: context, steps, test, done-criteria.

Working rules:

- Pick exactly one task from the plan. Implement, test, review, then move to the next.
- Do not start a new task while another is unfinished, unless the user explicitly redirects you.
- Update `specs/TASK.md` when you start and finish a task.
- When the work diverges from the spec, stop and surface the conflict to the user.

## Agent roles

Roles are defined in `agents/roles/`. The agent (or subagent) acting in a role follows that role file.

**Core roles (always active):**

- `agents/roles/orchestrator.md` — decomposes tasks, delegates, keeps the spec current
- `agents/roles/developer.md` — implements tasks
- `agents/roles/tester.md` — writes and runs tests, verifies acceptance criteria

<!-- IF:role_ui_designer -->
**Optional roles (enabled for this project):**
- `agents/roles/ui-designer.md` — designs and refines UI before implementation
<!-- ENDIF -->
<!-- IF:role_file_worker -->
- `agents/roles/file-worker.md` — bulk mechanical file operations on a cheap model tier
<!-- ENDIF -->
<!-- IF:role_code_reviewer -->
- `agents/roles/code-reviewer.md` — reviews every diff before commit
<!-- ENDIF -->
<!-- IF:role_devops -->
- `agents/roles/devops.md` — CI/CD pipelines, Dockerfiles, deployment config
<!-- ENDIF -->

## Testing policy

- **Framework:** {{test_framework}}
<!-- IF:tdd -->
- **TDD is on.** For every task: write the failing test first, implement until it passes, refactor. Never implement ahead of a failing test unless the user explicitly asks.
<!-- ELSE -->
- Tests are written after or alongside implementation; coverage of acceptance criteria is mandatory.
<!-- ENDIF -->
<!-- IF:coverage_gate -->
- **Coverage gate:** tests must not fall below {{coverage_gate}}% coverage; CI fails below it.
<!-- ELSE -->
- No fixed coverage gate; cover every acceptance criterion.
<!-- ENDIF -->

## Quality gates

- **Linter:** {{linter}} — run `{{cmd_lint}}` before every commit.
- **Formatter:** {{formatter}} — format changed files before every commit.
<!-- IF:review_before_commit -->
- **Review before commit:** show the user a summary of the diff before committing.
<!-- ENDIF -->
<!-- IF:security_review_on_request -->
- **Security review:** run a security-focused review of the diff when the user asks, before releases, or when touching auth, crypto, or input handling.
<!-- ENDIF -->

## Documentation

<!-- IF:changelog -->
- Keep [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) current while you work: record notable changes under `[Unreleased]` (Added / Changed / Fixed). Never leave a notable change unrecorded.
<!-- ENDIF -->
<!-- IF:adr -->
- Architecture decisions live in `docs/adr/`: copy `docs/adr/TEMPLATE.md` to `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md` and record the decision, its context, and its consequences. Never rewrite an accepted ADR — supersede it with a new one.
<!-- ENDIF -->
- Documentation is English only and lives next to the truth it describes.

## File conventions

- Specs and plans are the only place where requirements live — do not scatter them across code comments.
- Keep this file (AGENTS.md) current when rules, roles, or commands change.
- Directory map: `src/` (code), `specs/` (lifecycle), `agents/roles/` (role definitions), `.project-setup/` (setup record).
